rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The Approved List provides biological-agent classifications used under COSHH.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The list is approved by the Advisory Committee on Dangerous Pathogens.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The classifications support risk assessment and selection of appropriate control measures.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The list is relevant to deliberate work with biological agents in research, teaching, diagnostics and industrial processes.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: It is also relevant to work with humans or animals known or suspected to be infected.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The 2026 sixth edition reviewed existing hazard-group classifications.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The 2026 edition added previously unlisted agents to Hazard Groups 2 and 3 where appropriate.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: Advice on available vaccines was updated and users are expected to review changes affecting their controls.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: Biological-agent risk depends on the agent, hazard group, activity, route, dose, containment, worker susceptibility and available treatment.

rows.source: HSE Approved List of biological agents
rows.verified: The Approved List is agent-, laboratory-, task-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Safe systems for biological-agent incidents should cover cleaning, disinfection and disposal of contaminated waste.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Incident arrangements should include recording of accidents and exposures.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Medical advice should be available when the risk assessment identifies a need.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Releases of Hazard Group 3 or 4 agents may require accident or emergency response because severe disease could result.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Emergency procedures should be proportionate to the risk identified by the assessment.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Workers may need instant access to procedures that help contain an accidental release.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Accidents and dangerous occurrences involving biological agents must be reported under RIDDOR when reporting criteria are met.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Deliberate work with Hazard Groups 2, 3 and 4 and consignments of Hazard Group 4 agents require the applicable HSE notification or consent process.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: Deliberate biological work risk depends on agent classification, containment, procedure, exposure route, workforce, waste handling and emergency readiness.

rows.source: HSE safe deliberate work with biological agents
rows.verified: HSE biosafety guidance is agent-, facility-, activity-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level public-health probability.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: Employers must provide PPE free of charge when a risk assessment shows it is needed.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: PPE may include helmets, gloves, eye protection, hearing protection, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear and harnesses.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: Respiratory protective equipment is PPE used to reduce inhalation of dust, mist, gas or fumes.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: PPE is considered after engineering controls and safe systems of work have addressed risks as far as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: PPE must be assessed before use to confirm it is fit for purpose.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: PPE must be maintained and stored properly.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: Workers must receive instructions, information and training on safe PPE use.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: Employers must ensure PPE is used correctly and complies with applicable product-supply requirements.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: PPE performance depends on selection, compatibility, fit, condition, maintenance, wearer behaviour, task and exposure environment.

rows.source: HSE personal protective equipment at work
rows.verified: HSE PPE guidance is equipment-, wearer-, task-, hazard-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level protection probability.
